q: What is the definition of real estate?
What is the difference between real estate and real property?
a: Real estate refers to land and any permanent improvements attached to it, including buildings, structures, and natural resources such as minerals, water, and crops. Legally, real estate is distinguished from personal property, which includes movable possessions not permanently affixed to land. Real estate is a fundamental asset class that serves both as shelter and commercial space and as an investment vehicle that can appreciate in value over time.

q: What are the types of real estate?
What are the different categories of real estate?
types of real estate residential commercial industrial
a: Real estate is broadly categorized into five main types: residential (single-family homes, condominiums, townhouses, apartments, and multifamily dwellings where people live), commercial (office buildings, retail spaces, shopping centers, hotels, and restaurants used for business activities), industrial (warehouses, factories, distribution centers, and manufacturing plants), land (vacant lots, working farms, ranches, and undeveloped parcels), and mixed-use (properties that combine two or more types, such as a building with retail on the ground floor and apartments above). Each category has distinct market dynamics, financing options, valuation methods, and legal considerations.

q: What is the difference between freehold and leasehold?
a: Freehold ownership (or fee simple) is the most complete form of property ownership, granting the owner full rights to the land and buildings for an indefinite period, including the right to sell, lease, mortgage, or bequeath the property. Leasehold ownership grants the leaseholder the right to use and occupy a property for a specific period under a lease agreement with the freehold owner, but the leaseholder does not own the land itself. Leasehold properties are common in high-density urban markets and for certain commercial arrangements, with lease terms typically ranging from 30 to 99 years, after which possession reverts to the freeholder.

q: What is the MLS in real estate?
What does MLS stand for in real estate?
What is the Multiple Listing Service?
What is a real estate agent vs a broker?
What is the difference between a real estate agent and a Realtor?
a: The Multiple Listing Service (MLS) is a cooperative database of properties for sale created and maintained by real estate professionals to share listing information, enabling agents to find suitable properties for their buyers and giving sellers broader market exposure. Real estate agents are licensed professionals who assist in buying, selling, and renting properties, while brokers have additional education and licensing that allows them to work independently and hire agents. A Realtor is a real estate professional who is a member of the National Association of Realtors (NAR) and adheres to its strict code of ethics, distinguishing them from non-member agents and brokers.
